messages.author: 8b544cbd8df3ddb3
messages.subject: Standardized Residuals
parts:
Hello,

     Is it possible to get standardized residuals for each item in a scale, for each person? We ran a graded response model in mirt on a 5 item scale. Our understanding was that the "personfit" command computes the average of the standardized residuals across items for each person (e.g. infit/outfit). The "itemfit" command computes the average of standardized residuals for a given item, across all people. Neither though gets at standardized residuals for each item, for each person. 

     In case it informs anything, an approach we considered to calculate the standardized residual was following the formula below, where the numerator is the residual and the denominator is the variance of the observed response given theta. We had no problem calculating the residual, but how can we use mirt to calculate the variance of the observed response given theta? 

 


         Thank you,

          Ray

messages.author: 8b544cbd8df3ddb3
messages.subject: Re: Standardized Residuals
parts:
To clarify, we were wondering if there was a mirt analog to the IRT.residuals() function in TAM, which returns residuals and standardized residuals for each observation in a dataset to which a unidimensional IRT model was applied. 

Thank you,
Ray

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Standardized Residuals
parts:
Apologies for the long delay. This is now possible by using personfit(mod, return.resids=TRUE), which will now return a list containing the NxJ standardized and unstandardized residuals. Though note that this implementation is not limited to unidimensional models.

Phil
